title: Machine-translated strings must not be served until a human reviews them
description:
Migration b6d2f4a9c1e7 seeded 214 machine-translated strings with source='imported' -- the same value workbook-sourced strings carry. Nothing in the database distinguishes 'came from a deployed ODK form' from 'Claude wrote it', and approval is per-locale, so approving a locale blesses both at once. On the owner's dev database all thirteen locales are approved and active, which means unreviewed machine translations are being served to web forms right now.

Owner's intent, stated 2026-09-20: only the workbook-imported translations are approved; the machine-translated ones need review. They must remain visible and editable in the panel -- deletion is explicitly not wanted, because it removes the very content someone has to review.
design:
Third source value SOURCE_MACHINE = 'machine' (source is String(16), no CHECK constraint, so no widening needed).

1. Migration relabels the 214 seeded rows imported -> machine, matching on the exact literals from b6d2f4a9c1e7 so a row an administrator has already corrected or that no longer matches is left alone. Reversible.
2. export_translations excludes source='machine', so the served payload omits them and the client falls back to English per string -- the same mechanism an untranslated string already uses. This is the whole fix: the strings exist, are listed, are editable, and are not served.
3. The panel marks machine rows distinctly and offers an accept-as-is action that promotes machine -> edited without retyping. update_string already sets edited, so an admin who edits the text is already covered; the gap is only accepting a good machine string unchanged.
4. A workbook re-import must overwrite a machine row: workbook beats machine, while edited still beats both. Today the importer keeps edited and overwrites imported; machine must join the overwritable side.
5. Per-extension coverage should not count machine rows as translated, or the panel will report a locale as complete on strings that are not being served.
acceptance_criteria: A locale with machine rows serves English for exactly those items and its own workbook translations for the rest. The panel lists machine rows, marks them, and can promote one to edited. A workbook re-import overwrites a machine row and never an edited one. Coverage does not count machine rows. Tests pin each of these.
close_reason: Machine-translated strings are now a distinct source='machine', relabelled by migration c1a4b6e8d3f2, excluded from export_translations and from coverage, visible and acceptable in the panel via POST .../strings/accept. Precedence edited > imported > machine holds without importer changes (only SOURCE_EDITED was ever special-cased). Constraint renamed to ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved by d2b5c7f9e4a3 and the model now passes only the discriminator. Review found one real gap, fixed before commit: export_xliff labelled machine rows state='translated', so a CAT tool showed unreviewed drafts as finished; they now export as initial with subState digitva:machine, and an unmapped source understates rather than claiming translated.

title: Web form locale codes: column default 'en' is not a seeded mas_languages code
description: va_project_master.web_intake_default_locale defaults to 'en' (model and migration f2a9c4d7e1b3) but flask seed run creates mas_languages codes 'english', 'hindi', ... (app/commands/seed.py). Consequences on every seeded deployment: (1) the form-options resolver in app/routes/api/organization.py logs 'en is not an active language' and falls back to the first active code, so on dev every project's web form opens with locale='assamese'; (2) the projects admin panel now shows 'en (inactive)' and blocks Save until an admin picks an active code. Deeper question: the WHO VA web component's locale attribute expects instrument locale codes ('English (en)' in the bundle), not mas_languages codes, which exist for narration-language alias mapping. Decide: either seed short locale codes / add a locale_code column on mas_languages that the resolver serves, or map at the endpoint. Domain decision, not for an agent to take.
design: Decided 2026-09-19 with the owner: 'en' is the system default web-form language on every project and is always available; a project ADDS languages from the set the bundled instrument actually has translations for (an explicit registry in Python, asserted against the bundle by a test), not from mas_languages; the interviewer picks a working language on the intake page, remembered in the browser (localStorage, last choice wins), falling back to 'en' when the remembered code is not in the project's list. Narration languages stay on mas_languages: they describe the recording, not the screen. No migration.
close_reason: en is default everywhere; project adds instrument-translated locales; browser remembers the interviewer's choice. Suite 1,464 passed.

title: Report coverage against all translatable strings, not base question labels only
description:
Coverage is computed against reference_label_keys() -- 476 base question labels -- so every locale reports 100.0% while roughly a third of its translatable text is untranslated. Measured on dev 2026-09-20.

The reference holds 1,435 translatable items: 556 question labels, 340 guidance hints, 215 hints, 324 choice labels. Against that denominator every locale sits at 66-68%. Against all question labels including the DigitVA layers (556) they sit at 86-87%. Against the base-only 476 they report 100%.

Two defects, not one. The measure is too narrow: hints, guidance hints and choice labels are translatable, are served, and are invisible to the number. And the denominator is stale: base-only stopped being correct for labels the moment layer questions became translatable (digitva-thr), which is why Khasi reads 100% holding exactly 476 of 556 labels -- every base label, no layer labels.

Owner's instruction 2026-09-20: measure total translatable strings against translated strings.
design:
Headline coverage becomes translated / all translatable reference items, with the label figure kept as a breakdown rather than deleted -- both are useful, only one should be the headline. Per-extension coverage likewise counts every item kind, not just labels; extension_label_keys is label-only today and needs an all-items sibling.

Must exclude source='machine' rows once digitva-4kj lands, or the honest denominator gets a dishonest numerator.

Coverage still decides nothing (2026-09-19 decision stands): this changes what the number says, never what it gates.

Expect a documentation sweep, not just a code change: every claim that a locale is at 100 percent becomes false, including docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md, docs/current-state/admin-and-setup.md, cli-reference.md and handoff.md. The 'all thirteen documented languages reach 100 percent coverage on the survey labels' line in handoff.md is true only of the narrow measure and must say which one it means.
acceptance_criteria: locale_status and the panel report translated/total over all translatable items, with the label-only figure shown as a breakdown. Per-extension coverage counts all item kinds. machine rows count toward neither. A test pins the denominator at the reference's full item count so a future change to the reference cannot silently narrow it again. Docs no longer claim 100 percent without naming the measure.
notes:
Blocked on digitva-4kj: both change coverage computation in app/services/instrument_translation_service.py and the same panel and docs, so they must not run concurrently.

DOC SCOPE, measured 2026-09-20 rather than assumed -- it is small. Three places mention 100 percent and all three already name their measure: docs/current-state/admin-and-setup.md:313 ('base coverage (WHO survey labels, informational)'), handoff.md:220 ('100 percent on the base instrument'), handoff.md:340 ('100 percent coverage on the survey labels'). None is false; each is narrow. So this is not a sweep of wrong claims -- it is a change to which number is the headline, plus making these three say so explicitly. An earlier note on this bead implied a larger documentation problem; that was wrong.

VERIFIED PREMISE for the fallback these numbers describe: export_translations (app/services/instrument_translation_service.py, the questions/choices loop) builds its dicts only from rows that exist, so an untranslated item is ABSENT from the served payload rather than an empty string. Per-string English fallback is real, confirmed by reading the code 2026-09-20, not inferred from a report.

title: Decide whether a bulk re-import knocks an approved locale back to in_review
description:
The approval gate holds for a NEW locale but not for an existing one. An admin can re-import any workbook (the documented-source name gate was removed 2026-09-20) or POST an XLIFF hand-back into a live, approved, active locale: version bumps, every string can change, and the locale stays approved and keeps being served. Nobody re-reviews the new content.

digitva-j23's premise was 'incomplete, in-process or unverified translations must not be offered to users'. That is satisfied for a locale nobody has approved yet, and defeated for one that was approved before its content was rewritten. Found by audit 2026-09-20; import_translations, update_string and import_xliff contain no reference to lifecycle_state, which was implemented as specified and is correct as far as it goes.
design:
Two candidate rules, and this is a behaviour decision for the owner rather than a bug to fix quietly:

(a) A bulk rewrite of an approved locale sets it back to in_review, clears approved_by/approved_at and deactivates it. Safe, and noisy: a one-string correction via re-import would take a language off the forms.
(b) Bulk rewrites of a live locale are trusted, written down as a deliberate decision.

update_string is a different case and should stay as it is: an administrator editing one string IS the reviewer, so leaving the locale approved is defensible. The distinction worth drawing is bulk-replace versus single-string edit, not write versus read.
acceptance_criteria: Whichever rule is chosen is enforced in both import_translations and import_xliff, pinned by a test, and stated in docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md's lifecycle section.

title: Seed DigitVA-authored layer translations on a fresh install, not only via migration
description:
Migration b6d2f4a9c1e7 seeds 214 DigitVA-authored translation strings, but it inserts only where a mas_instrument_locales row already exists. On a fresh install no locale rows exist at migration time -- the operator creates them later by importing workbooks -- so a new deployment receives 0 of the 214 strings and alembic will never run the migration again.

Verified 2026-09-20 on an empty database: 0 rows inserted. Nothing else covers it: no migration or seed command creates locale rows (app/commands/seed.py does not touch locales or translations; the only MasInstrumentLocales constructor in app/ is _get_or_create_locale). And no import can supply these strings, because no source workbook contains them -- that is why the migration exists.

Consequence: a new deployment's locales sit permanently at 0/2 on digitva_core and abha with the shared 'Medical and death documents' heading missing, and the only cure is hand-editing 214 strings in the admin panel.
design: Move the 214 tuples to a committed data file and add one idempotent CLI -- flask instrument-translations seed-layers -- that upserts from it, insert-only, never overwriting an edited row. The migration keeps its literals for the already-deployed database, or is reduced to calling nothing and the runbook names the CLI as a mandatory post-import step on every install. Either way the strings must be documented somewhere an operator reads, not only in a migration docstring.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh install that imports its workbooks and runs the documented steps ends with the same 214 strings the owner's database has. Running the seeder twice changes nothing. An administrator's edited row is never overwritten.

title: Per-locale translation lifecycle: draft, in_review, approved
description:
A locale is served to interviewers once is_active is set, and nothing records that anyone reviewed it. Decided 2026-09-20 by the owner: incomplete, in-process or unverified translations must not be offered to users, and the decision should be recorded rather than held in an administrator's head.

Add lifecycle_state (draft | in_review | approved), approved_by_user_id (FK va_users.user_id, nullable) and approved_at (tz-aware, nullable) to mas_instrument_locales. Only an approved locale may be activated, enforced in set_locale_active AND as a CHECK constraint (is_active = false OR lifecycle_state = 'approved') so the invariant cannot be broken by a direct write. Leaving approved while active is refused: deactivate first. Entering approved records the approving user and timestamp; leaving it clears them.

Coverage still decides nothing (2026-09-19 decision stands) - it informs the human who approves.
design:
Migration is additive and reversible, chaining onto e1b6c9a3d7f4.

BACKFILL, decided by the owner 2026-09-20 (supersedes the earlier grandfather-to-approved sketch): every existing locale becomes lifecycle_state='in_review' AND is_active=false, approved_by_user_id/approved_at NULL. Nothing unreviewed is served. All thirteen currently-active locales stop being offered to interviewers on upgrade; forms fall back to English per string until an administrator approves each locale and activates it. This is a deliberate behaviour change, not an oversight, and must be stated in the migration docstring, the policy baseline and handoff.h

Measured context for the operator runbook (dry-run cross-check per locale, 2026-09-20): of 81 layer items, re-import alone leaves Hindi and Khasi 9 short, Odia 10, Marathi 15, Bangla/Kannada/Malayalam/Tamil 40 (social autopsy absent from their DS workbooks), and Arabic/French/Portuguese/Spanish/Swahili all 81 (the WHO multilingual workbook carries no DigitVA layer). digitva_core and abha are 0/2 in every workbook and are hand-translation for all thirteen.

Surface lifecycle_state, approved_by and approved_at in locale_status, the locales API, the admin panel (state badge; Activate refused unless approved) and the CLI. Browser-originated transitions enforce CSRF via X-CSRFToken.
acceptance_criteria:
Activating a draft or in_review locale is refused by the service and by the database CHECK constraint. A locale cannot leave approved while active. Entering approved records the approving user and timestamp; leaving clears them. Import and per-string edits never change lifecycle_state.

Migration: upgrade over existing data backfills every locale to in_review and is_active=false -- a deliberate mass-deactivation per the owner's 2026-09-20 decision (this supersedes an earlier draft of this field, written before that decision, which wrongly required the thirteen active locales to stay active). Because upgrade clears is_active, it must capture the prior active set and downgrade must restore it: verified 2026-09-20 on a scratch database, two active locales deactivated on upgrade and restored on downgrade.
notes: Coverage still decides nothing (2026-09-19 decision stands): it informs the human who approves. The CHECK constraint makes 'active implies approved' unbreakable even by a direct write.
close_reason: Per-locale approval lifecycle landed: lifecycle_state/approved_by_user_id/approved_at, CHECK constraint ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved, service/route/CLI/panel surfaces, migration a3f7c1d9e6b4 with a verified recovery path for the is_active flags it clears. Backfill is the owner's 2026-09-20 decision: every locale to in_review and deactivated, nothing unreviewed served. Two follow-ups filed rather than folded in: digitva-dqh (a bulk re-import of an approved locale does not knock it back) and digitva-dms (the seeded strings reach only an already-deployed database).

title: Stop parsing the policy doc to gate translation imports
description:
The importer reads docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md at import time (SOURCE_POLICY_DOC, instrument_translation_service.py:85) and refuses any workbook not named in its 'Translation sources' table for that locale. Decided 2026-09-20 by the owner: the table is a guide recording provenance; no code may depend on it. Importing a questionnaire source is a reviewed one-time activity, and the runtime path for changing translations is the admin string editor, not a re-import.

Remove documented_sources(), DocumentedSource and SOURCE_POLICY_DOC, and the rule that refuses an undocumented workbook. Keep: path containment, the sha256 and source_document recorded on the locale row from the file actually imported, and --cross-check as a dry run (report, write nothing). The 'Translation sources' table stays in policy as provenance, with an explicit note that no code reads it.
design: Watch language_name: if a new locale's display name was taken from the markdown table, it needs another source (the workbook's own language column, or an explicit argument). The locales API currently projects documented_source (tests/routes/test_instrument_translations_api.py:201); report the row's own source_document instead.
acceptance_criteria: No module under app/ reads a file under docs/ at request or import time. flask instrument-translations import accepts any readable workbook for any locale. --cross-check still writes nothing. Tests that asserted the refusal are rewritten to pin the new rule, not deleted.
close_reason: Removed the policy-doc parsing gate; importer now accepts any readable workbook under path containment. Tests updated and passing (98 passed).

title: Server accepts the client's own valid boolean as the questionnaire validity gate
description: app/services/web_intake_service.py:796-797 is the entire server-side form-validity check: 'if completion.get("valid") is not True: raise WebIntakeError(...)'. The server trusts a boolean the browser computed by running the TypeScript expression engine over the answers; it never re-derives validity from the relevant/constraint source strings that sit in the instrument JSON it already has. The only independent server checks are that Id10013 (consent) is answered and that the org unit is live (_require_live_org_unit). Verified 2026-09-20: no Python code anywhere parses or evaluates XLSForm expression grammar -- app/services/xlsform_instrument_builder.py:169-172 passes expression text through as opaque {source: ...} and says so in its module docstring; there is no pyxform/formpack/xpath dependency in pyproject.toml or uv.lock. So vendor/who-va-2022/src/engine/expression.ts is the single evaluator in the system and the browser is the sole enforcement point. Consequence: a client that sets valid=true can submit answers violating any constraint or relevance rule in the instrument. Whether that matters depends on the threat model for web intake (authenticated interviewers, not the public), which is the decision to take -- this bead is to make that decision explicitly rather than by default. Related but distinct from digitva-aiy, which is about relevance orphaning already-captured image answers. Pre-existing; found while auditing the blast radius of an expression-tokenizer change for digitva-thr.3.

Neither matches the implementation. title: Hidden-by-relevance answers are never cleared, so gate questions can orphan image slots
description: The instrument engine treats relevance as presentational: vendor/who-va-2022/src/engine/session.ts has no relevance-based answer clearing, so a question that becomes irrelevant keeps its stored value in the draft. digitva-thr added ds_available/md_available gates in front of the existing ds_count/md_count -> ds_im*/md_im* relevance, which widens the surface: an interviewer can now photograph document slots, then answer the gate 'no' or 'ref', and the image answers stay in the draft payload while the questions are hidden. Pre-existing mechanism (reducing md_count already did this), not caused by digitva-thr, but the gate makes it reachable in one step. Decide whether irrelevant answers should be cleared on submit, on relevance change, or left as-is and filtered at payload build. Note attachments phase 2 will make these real files, not just references, so settle it before then. Found by code review 2026-09-19.

title: CHECK constraint name is doubled and truncated in the database
description:
ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved is stored as ck_mas_instrument_locales_ck_mas_instrument_locales_act_5121. The metadata naming convention is ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s, and both the model (app/models/mas_instrument_locales.py:67) and migration a3f7c1d9e6b4 pass the already-prefixed full name as constraint_name, so the prefix is applied twice and Postgres truncates at 63 characters.

Create and drop are self-consistent, so nothing breaks today, and the schema-drift test stays green because alembic does not compare CHECK constraint names. But the name in the database matches neither the model nor the migration nor the docs, so anyone searching for the declared name will not find it.
design: Pass only the discriminator -- name='active_requires_approved' -- in the model, so the convention renders ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved. a3f7c1d9e6b4 is already committed and applied, so it must not be edited: a new migration renames the existing constraint (ALTER TABLE ... RENAME CONSTRAINT), with a downgrade that renames it back. Verify the post-rename name against pg_constraint rather than assuming.
acceptance_criteria: pg_constraint reports ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved. The constraint still refuses an active non-approved row after the rename. Schema drift stays green and upgrade/downgrade round-trips.
close_reason: Machine-translated strings are now a distinct source='machine', relabelled by migration c1a4b6e8d3f2, excluded from export_translations and from coverage, visible and acceptable in the panel via POST .../strings/accept. Precedence edited > imported > machine holds without importer changes (only SOURCE_EDITED was ever special-cased). Constraint renamed to ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved by d2b5c7f9e4a3 and the model now passes only the discriminator. Review found one real gap, fixed before commit: export_xliff labelled machine rows state='translated', so a CAT tool showed unreviewed drafts as finished; they now export as initial with subState digitva:machine, and an unmapped source understates rather than claiming translated.

title: Vendored vitest suite is timing-flaky under machine load
description:
On 2026-09-20, with the machine under sustained load (load average 4.27; the Claude desktop app alone at 77% CPU, Docker VM at 16.5% memory), the vendored package suite at vendor/who-va-2022 failed roughly two runs in three, with a DIFFERENT test failing each time:
- tests/web-audio-control.test.tsx > 'changes from start to stop and returns the saved recording' (vi.waitFor timeout, onAnswer never called)
- tests/web-validation-navigation.test.tsx:279 > 'scrolls to and focuses the first invalid question after Next' (expected vi.fn() called once, got 0)
- tests/web-component.tracer.test.ts > 'does not enable plaintext browser persistence by default' (expected undefined to be 'true')

The same suite passes 715/715 cleanly when the machine is quiet, including twice earlier the same day and once during this very investigation (run 1 of 3). A different test failing each run is the signature of timing flakiness, not a regression: a real defect would fail the same test deterministically. Vitest's own phase timings were several times their normal values during the failing runs (transform 30.7s, import 60.7s, environment 29.2s against ~3-15s normally).

Worth fixing because the suite is a release gate: if it fails two runs in three on a loaded developer machine, people will learn to re-run until green, which is exactly how a real failure gets waved through. The three tests named above all depend on async settling -- vi.waitFor, a focus/scroll side effect, and a tracer flag -- so the likely fix is explicit waits or fake timers rather than longer timeouts. Note the tracer one asserts a security-relevant default (plaintext browser persistence off), so it is the least acceptable of the three to leave flaky.

Observed while verifying digitva-thr.3/thr.4; not caused by them (the change in flight when it appeared was Python-only).

title: ODK site-mapping POST may not be idempotent under extreme latency
description:
Observed once on 2026-09-20 during a full-suite run under heavy concurrent machine load: tests/test_admin_api.py::AdminApiTests::test_odk_site_mappings failed with "'False' != 'True'". The test POSTs a mapping for (site_a, test_form) with form_smartvahiv='True', asserts the 201 response carries 'True' (that assertion PASSED), then GETs the mapping list and finds form_smartvahiv='False' for the same odk_form_id. The app's own slow_request log recorded duration_ms=151997.7 for the POST and 152010.1 for the GET -- roughly 152 seconds each. Suite wall time was 336s versus 115s on three earlier runs the same day.

Did NOT reproduce under normal load: the test alone passed 3/3, the whole file passed 45/45 three times, and the file combined with tests/services/test_instrument_translation_import.py passed 83/83, with no slow_request lines in any of the 7 runs. So this is not a regression from the digitva-thr.3/thr.4 work (which touched only the translation service and the vendored instrument) and the test is not deterministically broken.

Worth a look anyway because the failure shape is a read-after-write inconsistency, not a timeout: the write reported the right value and the immediately following read reported a different one. One hypothesis worth testing is that a POST retried under extreme latency creates a SECOND map_project_site_odk row for the same (site, odk_form_id) carrying column defaults, which the list endpoint's lookup then returns instead of the intended row -- i.e. the endpoint may not be idempotent and there may be no uniqueness constraint preventing a duplicate mapping. Check whether map_project_site_odk has a unique constraint on (site_id, odk_form_id) and whether the POST handler upserts or blindly inserts. If it blindly inserts, the same duplicate could be created by a double-click in the admin panel, not only by a pathological test run.
notes:
Second occurrence 2026-09-20, in a full-suite run on the translation-lifecycle tree. Same assertion: POST returns form_smartvahiv True, the following GET reads False.

This occurrence weakens the load hypothesis from the first one. The first failure came in a pathological run -- 336s wall time, individual requests logged at ~152s. This one came in a 146.9s full run, which is normal for this suite, with no slow_request lines. Isolated: tests/test_admin_api.py passed 45/45 three consecutive times immediately afterwards, and the test passed in two other full runs on the same tree.

So the sharper hypothesis is order-dependence or shared state inside the full suite rather than timeout pressure: something earlier in the full run leaves state that makes this read return the pre-write value. Worth running the full suite with -p no:randomly (if used) or bisecting the preceding test files rather than chasing timing. The changed code on this tree is the instrument-translation subsystem and app/schema_filters.py -- nothing touching map_project_site_odk -- so it is not a regression from that work.

title: geography extension flag is derived and served but has no consumer

The data ND01 collects as geography questions is server-injected instead (app/services/web_intake_service.py:721-723) per decision O4. Decide: either wire the intended consumer (if one was meant -- e.g. gating an org-unit picker or a geography display) or document the flag as informational-only so the 'gates content' claim in policy stops applying to it. The eight extension names are settled by the owner and geography stays one of them either way; this is about the flag's claimed effect, not its existence. title: Vendored bundle manifest built_at makes rebuilds non-reproducible
description: app/static/vendor/who-va-2022/manifest.json records a built_at timestamp, so every rebuild dirties the manifest (and its bytes/sha256) even when the emitted .js is byte-identical. That noise is what let the bundle at 926c212 diverge from its source unnoticed until a step-0 check caught it in digitva-thr (fixed in 7bf1d5f). Consider dropping built_at, or moving it out of the checked-in manifest, so 'git diff after rebuild is empty' becomes a usable invariant and could be asserted by a test.
